text: A point x with ||x||_1 > c*t lies outside the causal forward cone; the bound E_a(t,x)=min(1,C_a exp[-mu_a (||x||_1-a*v_hop(a)*t)/a]) correctly gives E_a<1, supporting causal separation.
Do not assume that causal order alone identifies the Minkowski metric or its scale; additional isotropy or normalization assumptions are required.

When a*v_hop(a) converges to c from above, the cone boundary shifts outward; when it converges from below, the cone boundary shifts inward. The rate of convergence determines whether the null envelope is attained exactly or only as a limit.

Compute the l1-radius and euclidean-radius-squared for a given (t,x) by evaluating ||x||_1 and ||x||_2, then apply the exponential bound to obtain E_a; the null envelope is the limiting value of E_a as the argument tends to zero.
Guard against silently assuming isotropy or sharp propagation; always verify the null boundary under the specific convergence rate of a*v_hop(a) to c.

The bound E_a(t,x)=min(1,C_a exp[-mu_a (||x||_1-a*v_hop(a)*t)/a]) defines a causal envelope only when a*v_hop(a) <= c. If the product exceeds c, interval_before becomes negative outside the light cone, violating causal order.
Do not assume isotropy or sharp propagation without explicit declaration. The l1 norm cone is not rotationally symmetric; results depend on coordinate choice.
When t = ||x||_1/c, the interval_before = 0 and the point sits on the null boundary. This is the only case where cone_order_preserved is guaranteed without additional metric assumptions.
Compute l1_radius and euclidean_radius_squared directly from the coordinate tuple; these are independent of the exponential envelope and serve as invariant anchors for the certificate.

Antiskill: rejecting any derivation that silently promotes the l1 bound to a Minkowski metric without explicit scale identification. The coefficient a in the exponent must be justified by physical scaling, not assumed unity.

The LR bound C_a exp[-mu_a(||x||_1 - a*v_hop(a)*t)/a] is only defined and non-trivial inside the forward light cone ||x||_1 <= a*v_hop(a)*t. Outside, the exponent becomes positive and the bound decays to zero, establishing no causal constraint.
Do not assume that causal order alone identifies the Minkowski metric or its scale. Without isotropy or sharp propagation assumptions, multiple metrics can satisfy the same causal order.

Null envelope evaluation: when ||x||_1 = t (null separation), the exponent vanishes and null_envelope = C_a. When ||x||_1 > t (spacelike), the exponent is negative and null_envelope → 0, indicating the bound does not constrain spacelike points.

Construct explicit counterexample fixtures by fixing c, t, x and dilation factor, then computing l1-radius, euclidean_radius_squared, interval_before, interval_after from the geometry of the light cone.
Antiskill: reject any derivation that silently assumes isotropy or sharp propagation without explicit license. All causal claims must be conditional on the convergence rate of a*v_hop(a) to c.
When ||x||_1 > c*t the point is spacelike; when ||x||_1 = c*t it is null; when ||x||_1 < c*t it is timelike. The bound E_a(t,x) respects this partition only if v_hop(a) is explicitly set to match c.
Compute l1_radius and euclidean_radius_squared directly from coordinate values; use the bound formula E_a = C_a exp[-mu_a (c - a*v_hop(a))/a] with matched c to determine null_envelope.
The l1 norm ||x||_1 = |x_1|+|x_2| defines the causal cone boundary in this discrete-pixel model; violation places the point outside the future light cone.
Do not assume that ||x||_1 <= c*t is automatically satisfied; explicitly verify the inequality for each fixture.
When ||x||_1 = c*t the point lies on the null envelope; the bound evaluates to C_a if the velocity scaling matches c exactly.
Do not set null_envelope = 0 when the point is on the null surface; the bound C_a is non-zero and must be reported.

Do not claim that dν_v/dt = 0 globally conserves defect density; the counterexample shows local balance with source terms can violate conservation.

The fixture H=[[0,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,0]], P=diag(1,0,0), ψ=(1,i,1) yields total defect density ν_0+ν_1+ν_2 = 2. Edge fluxes F_{0→1}=[1,0], F_{1→2}=[0,1] give net outflow 1, so total defect is not conserved: d/dt(2) = 0 but flux imbalance 1 ≠ 0 source. This is the counterexample to unconditional conservation.

In finite topological models, quotient_degree and codomain_degree are artifacts of the chain-map construction, not automatic invariants of the underlying geometry. Their values must be sourced from the model, not assumed.
Do not identify scalar additive curvature with an angle merely because both are called holonomy. The names are distinct; the mapping requires explicit construction.
